# GUÍA PARA CIVILES / CIVILIAN GUIDANCE [italic]Léala una vez. Leia uma vez. Read it once and keep it in mind.[/italic]
The garrison is here to keep the colony, its people and its works intact. On a quiet day you will see a patrol walk past the mess and nothing more. When the Commander raises the alert state, the rules below apply to everyone.
## EN UN PUESTO DE CONTROL / AT A CHECKPOINT - Alto means stop. Keep your hands where the sentry can see them. - Have your colony ID ready. Contractors also show a current work order. - Declare any firearm before you are searched. Weapons without a Colonial Marshal licence are confiscated and logged. - Do not photograph or record checkpoints, sentry posts or troop movements.
## TOQUE DE QUEDA / CURFEW - Curfew hours are posted on this board and called over the colony PA in three languages. - Movement after curfew needs a pass from Colony Administration or the garrison duty officer. Essential workers keep theirs on their person.
## CUANDO SUENE LA SIRENA / WHEN THE SIREN SOUNDS - Get indoors and away from windows. Stay there until the all clear. - Follow your block warden. Do not come to the garrison gate; it will be closed. - Shelter locations are listed by [netlink="Colony Administration" link="admin.colony.gov"].
## QUÉ REPORTAR / WHAT TO REPORT - Unattended bags, crates or vehicles. - Strangers asking about patrol times, the armoury or the landing pad. - Cut fences, broken locks, missing explosives or mining charges. - A gas alarm sounding, or a gas monitor that is dark, damaged or tampered with. Carbon monoxide has no smell; the monitor is your nose.
The garrison does not ask about your politics. It asks that you do not carry a rifle for anyone.
## LO QUE NO HACEMOS / WHAT WE DO NOT DO Troops do not collect debts, settle disputes between neighbours or enforce Company contracts. Take those to the Colonial Marshals or to Administration. Citizens of the United Americas needing consular help can reach the [netlink="UA embassy" link="embassy.ua"]. A complaint about a sailor goes in writing to the executive officer, in any of the three languages.
